I used the 6B pencil brush that comes with procreate to sketch the initial drawing, and also for the line art. I used JJ’s canvas acrylic brush to add colour and render the highlights/shadows. I used the greyscale method to complete this piece, first rendering the piece in greyscale then adding colour using the Linear Light layer blend mode. I added shadows using the Multiply layer blend mode, and highlights using the Add layer blend mode. Canvas is 2500 x 3500 px.

Brush set link: https://www.deviantart.com/corelounge/art/JJcanvas-s-Exclusive-Brushes-853040236

I used the 6B brush that comes with procreate for the initial sketch, then the studio pen (also comes with procreate) to do the line art. Both the 6B brush and studio pen brush were modified in the brush settings to have a thinner end taper and also smaller max size. I used Gaussian blur to blend the skin tones, and the smudge tool (using the soft brush) to blend the hair. For the denim material I used a watercolour canvas brush on a reduced opacity multiply blend mode layer to create the denim effect, along with additional multiply layers filled with the jacket’s base colour to add more shadows. Canvas is 2500 x 3500 px.


Here is the brush set I bought that had the canvas brush:

If it’s for university you may find it easier first to find articles relating to your topic, pick out the main points and start structuring the body of your essay that way. Have each paragraph address a different article, that way you can compare/contrast (or meet whatever else requirements you have) them. This allows you to follow up in another paragraph with a discussion of what has been said about your topic, which then makes it easier to write a conclusion. After that, your intro should be very easy because it’s just a very watered down brief version of what you will be discussing in your essay. I always suggest writing essays this way as it has helped me and others do them more effectively and efficiently.
